payload.why: 7.2 sets a governing-language rule: the Arabic Table 5-1 (Appendix A image) governs over the English translation (Appendix B). The governing Arabic differs in substance from the English. A person must record the precedence and the resulting content of Table 5-1 once the Arabic reading is approved.

Note ٢ prints 'الأرض الطبيعية قبل أعمال التسوية والردم' (natural ground before grading and filling). The height column heading prints '(متر فوق منسوب الأرض الطبيعية)'. Zone values ٢٥ and ٤٠ match the English 25 and 40. Note ٣ (30 days' notice before erecting any crane) matches English note (3). The differences are in notes 1 and 2 and the datum.

payload.text: The governing Arabic Table 5-1 (ADD-03 Appendix A) differs from the convenience English translation (Appendix B) in two places. (1) Scope: the Arabic note 1 applies the limits to permanent and temporary structures, including stacks, cranes and construction equipment, while the English note (1) covers permanent structures including stacks only. (2) Datum: the Arabic measures height from natural ground level before grading and filling, while the English measures from finished ground level after grading and filling. Because the Arabic governs (7.2), construction cranes and temporary works fall under the 25 m (Zone A) and 40 m (Zone B) limits, and fill depth counts against the limit. This affects crane and lifting planning (see Q21), the platform levels of tall structures, and the 7.3 notification of items over 30 m.
payload.short: Arabic Table 5-1 is wider and stricter than the English translation (temporary works and cranes; natural ground datum)
